alternate_names: Sri Swayambhu Varasidhi Vinayaka Swamy Devastanam, Kanipakam
deities: Sri Varasiddhi Vinayaka Swamy (Lord Ganesha, self-manifested/Swayambhu idol in a well of water, believed to be growing in size)

history.summary: One of the most famous Ganesha temples of South India, at Kanipakam village in Irala mandal, about 11 km from Chittoor and 68 km from Tirupati, on the banks of the Bahuda river. Legend: three brothers (one blind, one deaf, one mute) digging a well struck a stone from which blood gushed; the three were cured, and villagers found a Ganesha idol whose base could not be reached - the Swayambhu (self-manifested) deity. The idol sits in the well which is always full of water, and is believed to be growing in size. 'Kani' (wetland) + 'Pakam' (flow of water) gives 'Kanipakam'. The temple was built in the early 11th century by Chola king Kulothunga Chola I and expanded in 1336 by Vijayanagara emperors; it is administered by the AP Endowments Department with a 15-member trust board. It is famed as a 'Court of Truth' where people take oaths, believing lies are exposed before the deity. CSV ERRORS: the CSV 'state' column contains 'Chittoor' (a district name), not a state; the correct state is Andhra Pradesh. The CSV town 'Chittoor' is imprecise: the actual town is Kanipakam village (Irala mandal), 11 km from Chittoor. Note: one blog source says 'Chittoor district (now Tirupati district)' but the geocoder and most sources place Kanipakam in Chittoor district (verify current district after the 2022 reorganisation).

name: Sri Varasiddhi Vinayaka Swamy Temple
town_description: Kanipakam is a village in Irala mandal of Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh, about 11 km from Chittoor town and 68 km from Tirupati on the banks of the Bahuda river. A quiet agrarian settlement, it is dominated by this famous Ganesha temple and sees lakhs of pilgrims yearly, especially during the Vinayaka Chavithi brahmotsavam.
